notes.title: 09-26 Major Content Update 1
notes.content:
Hello, everyone! Maicha Here!

We've just released a brand-new version, marking the very first major update since Spirit X Strike launched. Thank you all for your support along the way! 

As mentioned in the previous post, the update highlights the following new content: Energy Assault, replacing the old colored attack mechanics, True Self Arena, the new Boss Rush mode, and Air Combo extensions, now all ground combos have a corresponding in-air version.

We've gone over the details before, so I won't repeat them all here. Honestly, the best way to get a feel for it is just to dive in and try it yourself.

Full patch notes is below for easy reference. If you run into any issues or have suggestions,  please feel free to join the official Discord  and reach out to me directly!

v0.600 PATCH NOTES

[New Features]
[olist]
 Energy Assault System: Replaces the old color signal mechanic. Enemies now gather different elemental Energies into specific body parts to unleash charged attacks. Each element has its own unique effect.
 Added tutorials throughout the story to explain the effects of each Energy type.
 True Self Arena: Unlocked through Meditation after clearing the story. Face off against a series of bosses in succession. Your run will be scored, and your best record will be saved.
 Added air combo versions for all ground combos. Triggering them works the same way: jump and attack airborne enemies.
 Stone Knight joins as a new elite enemy in Chapter 2. Extremely tough and without a stun gauge, it will provide a fresh challenge.
[/olist]
[Adjustments]
[olist]
 Improved the Spirit Mimicry move storage mechanism: when storing a move, its style will now also be stored and shown by icon color (blue/yellow/red for Dragon/Eagle/Tiger styles). When the move is unleashed, it will follow the stored style, meaning that even if you are currently in Dragon style, an Eagle style move stored will still be performed in Eagle style.
 Optimized the UI display of Spirit Mimicry: the move storage slots will now only appear when Spirit Mimicry is activated or when switching to Instant Spirit Mimicry.
 Revamped the combat UI with a more dynamic and layered look.
 Rocket Launcher Mob has been added as a new enemy in Chapter 1. Enemy compositions in certain encounters in Chapters 1 and 2 have also been adjusted.
[/olist]

notes.title: Publisher Sale & UPDATE 1 Preview - Enemy Energy System, Boss Rush
notes.content:
Hello fighters! Maicha here.

It’s hard to believe three months have already passed since Spirit X Strike launched. During this time, I’ve been busy addressing issues players encountered, while also preparing our very first major update. 

What really surprised me is seeing the wishlists still growing. Knowing that so many of you are excited about Spirit X Strike means a lot. Any anxiety or uncertainty I had before has been replaced by a steady sense of purpose, thanks to your clear feedback and support. I am deeply grateful for your patience and love!

The first major update is scheduled to roll out next week. Here’s a quick look at what’s coming. Also, starting September 15, Spirit X Strike will join the XD Publisher Sale at 10% OFF, lasting for three weeks until the Autumn Sale ends on October 6.


Enemy Energy System
The biggest change in this update is the removal of the much-criticized “colored attack” of the enemy, replaced by the brand-new Energy System.

This means now all enemies can charge up energy. Instead of showing a direct attack warning, enemies now have various power attacks, and some of them remain parryable. 

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/00d9c1acdb58aadaab86c8fe13bf8f9f0e1bee31.gif

Enemies may unleash power attacks after gathering energy, or concentrate it on specific body parts. In short, enemies now feel more "intelligent." You’ll need to watch out for their feints designed to bait your parries, and carefully observe where energy is gathering to anticipate their next move.

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/348eb07984dd6ff66be1fd04379efb75d601f852.gif

Depending on enemy type, there are also different elemental energies: Blood Energy, Stone Energy, Spirit Energy, and more, each carrying unique effects. The Energy System is still being expanded and refined, so expect even more depth going forward.


Boss Rush
Also arriving in this update is the new Boss Rush mode: True Self Arena. On a small island in his meditation, Carter will face off against every boss currently in the game in a row, a classic staple for action games.

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/0c3d8e56594765ffeed04a81a4411c17e7a07b39.gif

With the introduction of the Enemy Energy System, all bosses have been significantly rebalanced and now feature additional interactive mechanics to keep the fights fresh.

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/40ccaa087d2129ffc46023e87a541525794224e4.gif

Expanded Air Combos
As some of you may have noticed, I have a personal fondness for air moves. In a recent patch, I slipped in nine new air moves for the Tiger and Eagle styles, though you might not have caught them.
In this update, every ground combo will now have its corresponding air combo, increasing the variety of airborne combat.

https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/b6f98dc255dee0cb67c8526d512491bb05f0b024.gif
https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/7bb7dc6037c9e697f7d051efd5ed5be55c38ac22.gif

In addition, the early-designed boss Stone Knight has been re-tuned and added as an elite enemy in the main game. Enemy layouts in Chapters 1 and 2 have been adjusted and various bugs have been fixed to improve overall gameplay experience. More detailed update time and full patch notes will be shared in upcoming announcements.

If you have any feedback on this preview or encounter any issues in the game, please feel free to join the official Discord  and reach out to me directly!

The full patchnote is listed below for your reference. If you encounter any issues or have feedback during gameplay, feel free to join our official Discord server. We'll respond and fix things as soon as possible.

[olist]
 New Game+ option is now available when starting a new game. This includes inheriting special attacks, gold, and items. A confirmation will appear when overwriting an existing save.

notes.title: July 25 Update – New Air Moves & Practice Mode Options
notes.content:
Hello fighters!

In the past few updates, I’ve mainly focused on improving enemy combat feedback and behaviors, revisiting bosses chapter by chapter to adjust their stun, stagger, and related mechanics for a smoother and more responsive combat experience. With that round of fixes mostly wrapped up, I’ve finally had some breathing room to work on new content.

One thing I wanted to address was the similarity between air combos across the three styles. Even mid-air, I want each style to feel distinct. So in the  update, I've added 9 new air moves for the Tiger and Eagle styles, giving them more unique flair.

I've also expanded the Practice Mode with more customizable options, and made some performance optimizations for game stability when facing large numbers of enemies.

You can find the detailed patch notes below. If you encounter any issues or have any suggestions while playing, feel free to share them in our official Discord server. We’ll do our best to address them as quickly as possible.

V0.505 PATCH NOTES
[New]
[olist]
 Added 9 new moves to the Tiger and Eagle styles.
 Practice Mode Options: enemy selection, enemy aggression toggle, and infinite Spirit Gauge options.
[/olist]
[Adjustments]
[olist]
 Performance optimization: improved game stability when facing large numbers of enemies.
[/olist]

notes.content:
Hello fighters!
We’ve just released a new update that focuses on tuning the stagger mechanics for Kai, Stone Kai, and Eileen. We’ve also improved Stone Kai’s AI behavior to make the boss fight more engaging and better balanced. Full patch notes are below. If you encounter any issues while playing, please join our Discord to share your feedback, and I'll address them as soon as possible.

V0.503 Patch Notes
[Adjustments]
[olist]
 Adjusted stagger mechanics for Kai in Chapter 3: Spirit mimicry can now reliably trigger stagger
 Adjusted stagger behavior for Eileen in Chapter 4: Players can now follow up with combos after triggering small staggers
 Stone Kai (Chapter 5), Stagger & Stun System Overhaul:

 Non-glowing attacks can now trigger attack offset and stagger, heavy attacks in Carter’s combos can also trigger stagger
 Stone Kai’s stun threshold has been lowered
 Carter now deals proper stun damage while Kai is staggered
 Spirit mimicry now correctly applies stun damage to Kai
 Final execution will only trigger if Kai’s HP is below 40% and he is stunned; otherwise, a normal Super Strike will occur
 Defeating Stone Kai now requires a final execution

 Carter’s hit recovery timings adjusted: All hit reactions can now be canceled slightly earlier for smoother responsiveness
 Spirit Mimicry healing adjustment: Healing amount is now affected by the amount of Spirit gauge when activated
[/olist]
[Fixes]
[olist]
 Fixed a bug where Kai could be knocked out of bounds in Chapter 3
 Fixed ground collision issues in the Chapter 5 environment
 Fixed an issue with camera blur effects and improved overall game stability
 Fixed incorrect animations for super stike and throw counters in Chapters 3, 4, and 5 boss battles
[/olist]

notes.title: June 26th Update: Motorcycle Enemy Adjustments, New Camera Sensitivity Slider
notes.content:
Hey Fighters! I've just pushed a new update, introducing more settings options as you suggested, allowing adjustments for camera sensitivity, combat music volume, and more. The motorcycle mobs have taken another whack, as an effort to reduce the frustration their non-stop attacks bring.

Since launch, I've been carefully reading all of your discussions about the game, the love, criticisms, and suggestions. These discussions help me brainstorm how to address the various issues. However, it's crucial to avoid rushing things; a step-by-step approach is necessary to bring out the true potential of Spirit X Strike. Thank you for being so patient.

1.New windowed/fullscreen toggle, invert camera Y-axis, camera sensitivity, and music volume adjustment in the settings.

[Adjustments]

2.Modified the mechanism for knocking motorcycle enemies off their vehicles: in-air attacks and successful dodge counters can now directly dismount them.

5.Corrected the amount of Spirit gained from hitting enemies with Active Spirit Dash; Spirit consumption for Active Spirit Dash has been increased.

2.Fixed a bug where Spirit Dash attacks would pass through motorcycle enemies.

If you encounter any issues while playing, please join our Discord to share your feedback, and I'll address them as soon as possible. For anyone experiencing game crashes upon launch, please also submit your specific hardware information to assist me in debugging. I am actively working on a solution, really appreciate your help!
This is Maicha, until next time!

notes.title: Difficulty Adjustment, Custom Settings, EA Release & Update Roadmap | Dev Blog#6
notes.content:
Hello, fighters! Maicha here.

We’ve just wrapped up the latest round of our closed beta, and I’ve been busy sorting through all the feedback these past few days. Seeing you all discussing boss strategies intensely, and reading all the lengthy, thoughtful feedback, it really hit me how much you care about what we’re building. Thank you so much for your participation and support!


Difficulty Adjustments & Custom Settings
The core content for the Early Access version is nearly complete, the focus now is on fine-tuning the game. Based on the recent invaluable playtest bug reports and feedback, I’ve been implementing solutions. In this dev blog, I want to address the biggest topic you’ve all raised: game difficulty. It’s not only our beta testers saying this, but demo players as well. The updated demo added three difficulties (that’s all but the hardest difficulty), and most players have told us the game feels too hard, too hard to be called Apprentice and Master.

In past updates, my main approach was to ease the requirements for triggering special moves. After talking with many of you, I realized that the real pain points come down to things like “multiple enemies attacking at once, no time to react,” “boss fights drag on for too long,” and “combat has a very low margin for error.” Since the root causes of difficulty are complex, I need to address them from multiple angles:

1. Enemy AI Behavior:

I’ll be rebalancing AI across all difficulties. On Apprentice and Master, Yellow attacks will track you less aggressively, and bosses will have optimized stagger mechanics, making it easier to have them staggered. Overall, boss fights should feel more manageable.

2. More Sufficient Resources:

I’m increasing the number of items you can pick up in-game, more healing and recovery items to give you a bit more room for error.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/cf74ef9fd56bc51f607877e3b678d7a304c48898.gif"]

PS: The frustrating motorcycle “bosses” are now back to the minions they should be.



Although Spirit X Strike is about that fast, high-octane action, it mixes in some fighting-game strategy: neutral, spacing, and countering, etc. I know that different players need different pacing. To help with that, on Apprentice and Master difficulties, I’ll introduce “Combat Assist” (turned off by default). When enabled, you get a brief “Za Warudo”-style time-stop effect right before getting hit, giving you a moment to react. That way, you can have a more forgiving experience if needed.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/727501b95b2b7503aec938f33c524c3da07ffe85.gif"]

I’ll also be polishing some basic quality-of-life settings: options to turn off motion blur, and key-binding customization if you need to replace the current default layout.


What to Expect in Early Access, Release Format, and the Future of Spirit X Strike
Right from the start, I mentioned that Spirit X Strike would launch in Early Access, and our players haven’t really questioned that. On one hand, you trust me even though this is a niche project; on the other, fans of old-school action games are usually savvy about Steam’s Early Access process.

I do still want to clarify that, Spirit X Strike has a clear schedule and I believe it meets Steam’s Early Access criteria: it’s “unfinished” (I’m transparent about this fact), it has a proficient gameloop in its current state, and I have a solid roadmap for continued development through to a final release.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/b311bf8b86407585772c170f838711acbde9ac7b.png"]



a solo developer who plans, Spirit X Strike’s future updates are mapped out from day one. Once the six chapters in Early Access are out, I’ll jump right into designing and developing the final two chapters and bosses, along with new game modes. I’m aiming for one major update per quarter, so within six months I hope to reach my envisioned “version 1.0.”

To keep everyone updated, I’ve put together a small roadmap showing the detailed update schedule and exactly what’s included in the Early Access build. Feel free to check it out!

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/f3c12e2df1957b1632ec237905bdf1be572f0219.png"]
On the Art & Environment Quality
Many of you have pointed out that the models and environments feel rough around the edges. I really appreciate your love and support over the years, even when some videos and streams called out “poor visuals.” Some people have suggested I find investors to improve the graphics (Like anybody would invest in it lol).

Spirit X Strike is, at its core, a completely solo-developed indie 3D action game. That means with a limited budget, I could only focus on the meat and bones for this game, which is the stylish, high-octane combat that delivers pure action-game excitement. That’s all I’ve ever aimed for, and your love for this style of game is why this project exists.

Currently, I'm polishing the later stages of Early Access content. And I’m thrilled to share that Spirit X Strike will be featured at the PC Gaming Show on June 8! During next week’s livestream, I’ll reveal the Early Access release date and some brand-new updates. Thank you again to everyone who has played the demo and participated in the playtest. Let’s keep up the Spirit (wink) and punching forward together! (ideally together on Discord)



PC Gaming Show Livestream Link:

[dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YXC7hf6PBTE"][/dynamiclink]

notes.title: May 23 Demo Update: New Boss & Scoring System
notes.content:
Greetings, fellow Spirit fighters! Maicha here.

Last week, we started the recruitment process for our beta test, and the response from players around the world blew me away. I honestly thought I’d struggle to find playtesters after being quiet for so long. Thank you all for sticking with Spirit X Strike! During the beta, I will try to drop a few more tester slots on our https://discord.gg/gjhmdzdfM6 from time to time. So welcome to hang out in our lair.
Sharp-eyed players may have already spotted Spirit X Strike on the PC Gaming Show event page, so let’s not keep it a secret any longer: the game will be featured in the PC Gaming Show on June 8, where we’ll be sharing some exciting new updates.

With the beta test underway, it’s now time to push a new demo out. I’ve made a bunch of tweaks and fixes to it. You can find them in the detailed patch notes below.
The demo covers most of the Prologue of the Early Access version (the only thing missing is the highest difficulty) and adds a brand-new boss fight against Bloody Sword. She’s the dual-blade and kicking specialist you may have caught glimpses of in the trailer and other posts, and can be quite a challenge to defeat. Trust me, even I can’t “no damage” her yet!

This demo will also introduce a scoring system: you’ll get graded on completion time, damage taken, combo count, etc., at the end of each level. Looking forward to your feedback on this new demo, and feel free to share your outstanding gameplay moments on social platforms!

notes.title: Back from GDC: Addressing Your Feedback
notes.content:
Hey, fellow Fighters, DaMaicha here. Just got back from GDC with loads of feedback from seasoned players and veteran developers. Ever since I started the development of Spirit X Strike, I’ve spent most of my time tinkering on my own. So being able to soak in the lively, vibrant development atmosphere was truly priceless.

While fighting off jet lag, I’ve paused the game cutscene development and tried to focus back on adjusting gameplay issues.With this Dev Blog, I’d like to quickly address some of the feedback I got.

Core Combat & Interactions
I noticed that many players prefer using parry as a safe way to initiate an offense. Some mentioned that the usual dodge doesn’t seem to be an effective option. “It doesn’t effectively evade close-range attacks or break off enemies’ tracking attacks, making it feel a bit pointless compared to simply parrying”.

Right now, both dash and jump come with a brief invincibility window at the start. I’ll look into it and
extend these windows to be more reasonable. I’ll also tweak the enemy’s yellow attack tracking and frequency to offer more options for defence and dodging.

Also, the inability to switch targets while locked on an enemy is due to the work-in-progress camera control. This affects the target switching function, that’s why I had to disable it in the build at GDC.

Some of you also found it hard to use the spinning kick to interact with weapons on the ground, this is due to the move’s target locking mechanism not being differentiated from other attacks. I’ll adjust the spinning kick’s offset and locking logic.

Boss Battles
Many players who challenged the first stage boss have mentioned this: “I can keep trying, but can we skip the mobs?”

Absolutely, my friends! The current checkpoint, where you have to fight the mobs again after respawning is just a temporary setting. In the launch version, you’ll continue to the boss fight directly. 😂

Also noted that the first boss’s charging felt unfair. I’m planning on adjusting the start-up time to make it more reactable, and changing the animation to make it more regenizable. 

Camera
As expected, the camera still sxxks. I was focusing on developing new content, so I apologize for not preparing a better optimized camera system.

Currently, moves like Super Strike don’t have enough pre-set camera angles, which results in forcing weird camera angles in many situations. Here’s my plan: first, to provide more varied pre-set camera angles, and second, have the game choose the right animation based on your current camera state when triggering Super Strike or other interactive skills. 

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/4d1f7469d439ca61e9cc45b6e34e1d04e5aa2336.gif

I’ll also fix the camera reset logic so that if the camera gets squished into an extreme angle and you lose sight of your character, it will quickly auto-adjust.

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/9c815d5ad10023076f20fc2df18dce6986f5bf2a.gif

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/b914d515e5cb0a2db92d3c457e7c1681da593040.gif
Levels and Tutorials
The tutorial is also a bit rough in the GDC demo since the overall flow is still being fine-tuned. But the final version will lean more toward interactive teaching, similar to the QTE-like tutorial you saw in the Next Fest demo. Once the tutorials are completed, there’ll still be a tutorial option in the menu for you to revisit the combat tips you’ve learned.

I really wanted to showcase as many new gameplay elements as possible during GDC that aren’t in the Steam demo. So some details were rushed, and there were quite a few bugs. I truly appreciate everyone’s patience and understanding. I’ll be working hard to fix all the issues as soon as possible. 🙏🙏

Here are some photos from GDC! Compared to the many outstanding games on display, Spirit X Strike seems a bit rough around the edges. But seeing the basic-looking booth surrounded by you all reminded me why I love developing this game. Let’s prove the good old Action Game genre is not outdated together!

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/6cb74c5c1762dfd2856e1942f14782e87b14f826.jpg
https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44461563/a74b5025813b7da654ff2a912dd26ade1b93bc11.jpg
Also, please come to our Discord to leave your feedback. They improve the game so much, and that will mean a lot to me. Until then, see you next time.

notes.title: Dev Blog #4: Parry-Counter Iron Wall Combat Style, Super "Claw" Strike, and More
notes.content:
Long time no see, fellow fighters, Maicha here! I just finished my Chinese New Year holiday. In the last dev blog, we discussed the weapon interaction system and introduced some new moves. We also communicated the decision to delay the release. I sincerely appreciate everyone’s understanding and support. The extra development time has been invaluable, and now it's time to update you on my recent progress through this dev blog.

Parry and Counter Combo: New Combat Style, "Iron Wall"
The new combat style "Iron Wall" is here. Using this style, Carter will fight only with his fists in a real sigma way. As the name suggests, this style significantly enhances the character’s defense.
But this defense can also be an offense. By predicting the direction of an enemy’s attack and adopting a specific defensive stance, you can trigger a powerful counterattack, and even neutralize the enemy’s red-glow unblockables.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/6a38ebfb8aa94a9e586b844b9947447163701a33.gif
Super "Claw" Strike and Double Super Strike
With the “Iron Wall” combat style, Carter uses a "fist and claw" combination for attacks and unlocks corresponding super strike. Like this “Tornado Claw” that can redirect the enemy’s attack and rip them apart.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/dc635fdcac979ebe8e3c9d231c32c2e1861d259c.gif
Additionally, this style offers a Double Super Strike that provides another way to deal with multiple enemies. When two enemies are simultaneously stunned and positioned closely, Carter will be nice and “hook” them up. Make them two have a little kiss.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/9d67c49b9ebab48b72885e460245498868f4e97c.gif
In addition to the default combat style and the previously introduced nimble style, which focuses on kicks, the Iron Wall style, emphasizes parrying and counterattacks using punches and claws, making it that there are three styles players can choose and switch at ease during combat. Each has its unique move set and super strikes, allowing players to tackle all types of enemies and create their own combos. This will make the character’s move set over three times larger than the original version.

Though I’ve heard some concerns about the development progress, I want to assure everyone that while Spirit X Strike is my solo-dev project, I have put efforts into developing it for over three years. Especially since the official announcement and the demo release, I’ve had the opportunity to communicate with all of you directly and this significantly improved my productivity in keyframe implementations and optimization.

Although there isn’t a release date yet, the development of the game is nearing its conclusion. We expect to have more testing schedules and updates to share next month. Players interested in testing can join our discord in advance. Also, feel free to share any thoughts or feedback about this dev blog there. More info is available on X:@SpiritXStrike, feel free to check out. And see you next time!

notes.title: Dev Blog #3: Weapon Interaction System, New Moves, and a Release Update
notes.content:
Hello, Fighters! This is DaMaiCha here. Today, I want to share some updates on the Weapon Interaction System and New Moves that we’ve been working on. But before that, let’s talk about the release schedule.

A Word on the Release Date
Since the Steam Next Fest ended, Spirit X Strike has welcomed over 10,000 new players adding the game to their wishlists. We’re now over 20,000 wishlists—an incredible milestone for which I’m deeply grateful.
I know this number reflects the faith and encouragement you all have for the game’s potential, and the feedback from the demo has given me so many ideas for further optimization. Looking back, the original plan to release by the end of this year feels a bit rushed. While no amount of time can close the experience and technical gap between Spirit X Strike and major titles, I still want to make the game the best it can be.
For that reason, I’ll be taking a little more time and aiming for a 2025 release. I hope you’ll understand, and I truly appreciate your patience and support as I keep refining the game.

Weapon Interaction System and Special Moves
In Spirit X Strike, the protagonist Carter is a “faithful warrior” who believes in smashing bullets with his fists and splitting the earth with his kicks. But when facing weapon-wielding enemies, Carter can adapt and respond with special weapon interaction skills—turning the enemy’s own attacks against them.
Special Moves are skills that can be used at any time. For example:

 When enemies attack with ranged weapons, you can trigger a Spinning Kick at the right moment to deflect projectiles back at them.
 In the full version, weapons dropped by stunned or defeated enemies won’t just disappear (as they do in the demo). Instead, you can kick them back into the fight.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/5515d2c94e360946317a76492099f17094cfb033.gif
Different weapon interactions will produce unique effects:

 Throwing Axes: Stun enemies for a short duration.
 Machetes: Deliver heavy damage and launch enemies into the air.
 Machine Guns: Carter can deflect bullets and use them to trigger abilities like the Spirit Dash.

More interactive enemy weapons will be added in the future to keep combat dynamic and exciting. You’ll be able to incorporate these weapon interactions into your combos and adapt them to the flow of each battle.

New Moves in Progress
In addition to the Weapon Interaction System, we’re also developing some brand-new moves.
The Spinning Kick I mentioned earlier is not just for reflecting weapons—it’s also a new combat move that can be integrated seamlessly into combos. Inspired by traditional sweeping kicks, this move can sweep enemies off their feet, leaving them vulnerable to follow-up attacks. Players can also capitalize on this by launching an enemy into the air for mid-air combos.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/ba012167810945aa1b2dc16902accffe0525ac3e.gif
Another new addition is the Rolling Grab Launcher. Triggering a Spirit Dash will allow Carter to grab the enemy, into a rolling attack, then launch them to the air before smashing them back down with a heavy punch.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/0a67f1659f67a0fe74b60319edfc5ab0a42a74e2.gif
If you’re curious to see these updates in action, I’ll share more clips of the moves in development on the Spirit X Strike X account. As always, I welcome any feedback—every comment you share helps me improve Spirit X Strike. Please share them in the official Discord!

notes.title: Demo Update - Camera & Combat Changes
notes.content:
Hello everyone! As I mentioned in the last DevBlog, I've been hard at work making a series of adjustments to the camera and the game's difficulty settings. Today, I'm excited to roll out an update to the demo version. Please download the latest update and see the changes for yourself!

PATCHNOTE
Adjustments
[olist]
 Camera Adjustments

 When not locked on, the camera now dynamically adjusts to ensure nearby enemies are within the player's field of vision.
 During lock-on or boss fights, the camera will center on the midpoint between the player and the enemy, ensuring both are always visible.

 Enemy Attacks and Alerts

 Melee enemies will now only attack if they are within the player’s field of vision; if out of sight, they will move into view before attacking. We've also refined the alerts for ranged enemy attacks.

 Block, Dash, and Jump Mechanics

 Blocking now nullifies all attacks if there is enough stance gauge.
 Dashes and jumps are given full invincibility frames, allowing players to avoid any attack if timed correctly.

 Expanded Input Windows for Perfect Guard and Instant Counters
 Boss Mechanics - "Invasion Squad Captain"

 Adjusted hit reactions for the first phase: If the boss is staggered by a powerful attack or counter, players can continue the offense and convert the stagger into a combo. If players successfully launch the boss into the air, airborne combos will ignore the combo hit limit. (The boss will recover after a certain number of hits on the ground)
 Reduced stun values in the first phase to allow multiple super strikes; the second phase will trigger only after the boss's health drops below a certain threshold.

 Pause Menu now includes an option to reset to the current checkpoint.
 Tweaks to running and forward jumping animations and speeds.
 Adjusted scene lighting and color tone for an improved visual experience.
[/olist]
New Additions
[olist]
 Added Japanese language support.
[/olist]
The current version is not yet the ideal and final state, and I will continue to improve it based on your feedback.If you have any feedback after trying the new version, please share it in the official discord! I'm super excited to hear your thoughts and continue improving Spirit X Strike together!

notes.title: DevBlog #2: [Camera & Difficulty Adjustments] [New Boss & Combat Style]
notes.content:
Hi everyone, MAICHA here! Although the Steam Next Fest has wrapped up, many new players are still trying out the demo and sharing feedback. In addition to continuing development, I’ve gone through all your survey responses. A huge thank you to everyone for participating—every single suggestion has been read with care.

The purpose of the demo was to let players experience the combat firsthand and to gauge reactions. I have noted all your feedback, especially the ones on camera control and difficulty, and I totally understand why these areas are a focus. Both are essential to the game experience, and I’m actively working on the solutions. I’ll go over here along with some of my plans moving forward.

It’s motivating to see players having fun in the combat, which gives me even more drive to keep improving. Thank you all again for your patience!

Camera Adjustments
Since different fights require different focal points, I’ll be adjusting the camera accordingly.

 For crowd battles, where players need to track multiple enemies and monitor positioning, the camera will no longer remain centered on the player. Instead, it will adapt dynamically to keep both the main enemies and the player within view—think of a Devil May Cry or Ninja Gaiden dynamic camera. This aims to reduce the issue players encountered in the demo with off-screen attacks.
 For boss battles, the camera will focus on the midpoint between the player and the boss, similar to Naruto Ultimate Ninja Storm or Dragon Ball Z Kakarot, allowing for smoother 1-on-1 combat. In a future chapter, this style will be applied to the duel between the main character, Carter, and his master, Aileen, creator of the Spirit Strike martial art. Here’s a sneak peek of this in action (still in testing!).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/adf9643bfb4f1340b0bc8e9e333122038ee5d3ef.gif

To address reports of motion sickness from certain animations, I’ll be adding more appropriate framing during Break effects and Super Strikes, avoiding forced camera angles, and minimizing drastic shifts. Sensitivity adjustments, motion blur toggles, and other camera settings will be available in the full release.

Game Difficulty
Spirit X Strike was designed from the start to be a hardcore action game, but the high difficulty reported by many players seems rooted in certain details that need fine-tuning. As discussed in the previous dev blog, adjustments are underway to refine enemy AI and expand the parry window.

More details here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2538880/view/4508758024141295366

The bigger change will involve the defensive moves. Currently, blocking, dodging, and jumping are set up as specific counters. Moving forward, they’ll all have invincibility frames, allowing players to avoid all attacks when timed correctly. Red and yellow indicators will simply serve as warnings for dangerous moves, making defense more flexible.

Boss Mechanics
Bosses will no longer have constant hyper-armor. Perfect parry, cross-counter follow-ups, and well-timed attacks during boss recovery will allow for longer combos. Boss stun meters will also be reduced, allowing players to trigger Super Strikes multiple times in a single fight. I’m also revising enemy defense mechanics to offer more options for guard breaks to increase positive feedback during combat. Feel free to share your ideas and suggestions on our official Discord!

Since everyone experiences difficulty differently, I’ll be adding a dynamic difficulty prompt. After repeatedly failing an encounter, players will be prompted to temporarily lower the difficulty. Additionally, a system similar to FF16’s assist mode is being considered, with a short slow-motion effect before taking hits, giving players more time to react. This feature will be optional.

The much-requested move list will be included in the full version. Since it ties into the upgrade system, it wasn’t included in the demo. I’m also addressing reported bugs one by one, and some critical issues will have safeguards to prevent them from forcing the player to restart the game, minimizing the frustration.

When Punches & Kicks Collide: New Boss, New Combat Style
As for development progress, I’ll be moving forward with designing new bosses, skill upgrades, and the surrounding systems for later chapters, saving the cutscene work for last. Here’s a new look at the gameplay I’ve been working on.

Those who joined earlier playtests may remember Kai, one of the first bosses designed for the game. In the story, Kai is both a friend and rival to Carter, and I wanted their fight to emphasize high-speed, fist-to-fist action—a thrilling back-and-forth exchange that action fans will recognize!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/31881c71ee2a7c96dcf10a62352cd793f797c939.gif

This punch-heavy fighting style gave me an inspiration: what if the main character could fight with hands in his pockets, using only kicks? Enter a new, stylish kicking combat style (still trying to figure out the name for this), where Carter fights enemies with only kicks. Players will be able to unlock special Super Strikes like “Scooter” or “Lightning Rapit Kick.”

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44461563/bb4b0523b83e85bfbce8943ea7ca31af01bfaece.gif

Adjusting based on feedback from the Next Fest has proven to be a bigger task than expected, so it may take some extra time. I’ll keep sharing updates on development progress here. Thanks, everyone, for sticking with me on this journey! Remember to join the official discord to share your thoughts with me!

notes.title: Spirit X Strike Demo Now Permanently Open & Survey
notes.content:
Hello, players! Over the past week of the Steam Next Fest, more than 10,000 players have tried the demo and added it to their wishlists. Thank you so much for your passion!
Since action games are best experienced firsthand, after consideration, the DEMO will remain open even after the fest ends. Whether you're a new or returning player interested in fast-paced combat or hardcore fighting games, feel free to dive back in anytime!
I’ve also prepared a feedback survey to gather your thoughts on the demo. Your feedback is highly appreciated, and I look forward to hearing from you!

Survey Link: https://forms.gle/AWiHgv3ehfjm6kTu6


During the Steam Next Fest, many players shared videos and content about the game. Seeing fellow action game enthusiasts discuss Spirit X Strike has truly felt like a dream come true. My original goal with this project was to create the pure action game I had always envisioned. The fact that it has resonated with others has been both surprising and humbling.

FAQs
Q: Which engine was the game developed with? Was it really made by just one person?
A: The game was developed using Unreal Engine 5. Many people are surprised or even skeptical that it was made by one person. But to be honest, what you see now—though still rough—represents my work over the past two years.
As a hardcore action game player myself, I know that making a great action game requires both solid technical groundwork and countless adjustments. However, since this is a solo project, I’ve had to focus on the core combat experience—including action design, animation setup, and keyframe implementation. Other aspects might not be perfect, but I’ve tried my best to keep things immersive. Thanks again for your patience and understanding!
P.S. The music and sound effects still need improvement. I plan to collaborate with professional sound designers on that in the future. I also want to thank the voice actors who helped bring my over-the-top script to life!

Q: The parry window feels too short. Will it be adjusted?
A: Yes! The timing for parries, dodges, and other counter mechanics will be made more forgiving in future updates. In fact, I’ve already made minor adjustments in last week’s patch, so be sure to check it out.

Q: Will there be a target lock or camera lock feature?
A: Yes, the lock-on system will continue to be optimized. I’m working to make the camera feel more modern, including smoother target switching.

Q: How will you address enemies attacking off-screen or bosses starting attacks without wind-up animations?
A: We’ll adjust enemy aggression levels based on difficulty settings and add visual cues and camera protections to help players anticipate incoming attacks.
As for bosses, the lack of wind-up animations (or overly short telegraphs) is something I’m aware of. I’ll be adding transition animations and lengthening wind-ups to make their attacks easier to read. I’ll also tweak boss stagger mechanics so players feel rewarded when successfully countering or interrupting their attacks.

Q: How is the game’s development progressing?
A: The vision for Spirit X Strike has always been clear: after laying a solid foundation, the goal is to steadily build out the combat system and story. Besides the demo, the game will include five chapters during its Early Access phase. So far, I’ve completed the first two.

I’ll continue to adjust the combat system and gameplay balance based on feedback from the demo. If you want to follow the development progress more closely, feel free to join our Discord community! We also plan to organize more demo playtests in the future.

Thanks again for playing Spirit X Strike!
